text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- U.S ratings institutes Moody's Investors Service and A.M. Best put insurer Aegon's credit rating on their watchlists. (p1)
- Dutch businessmen look at possible bid for bankrupt aircraft maker Fokker, after South Korean industrial conglomerate Samsung announced it is definitely pulling out. (p1)
- Port of Rotterdam forecasts stronger growth of container transshipment than originally expected despite slight decline in 1996. (p1)
- Financial services group Achmea boosts 1996 net by 21 pct to Dfl 570 million. (p3)
- Telecom arm of Dutch PTT (KPN) starts own internal temp agency. (p3)
- Food maker Koninklijke Smilde books lower 1996 net on Dfl 650 million turnover. (p3)
- EOE-options exchange leaves European rivals far behind with 69 pct turnover growth in 1996. (p9)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Broker Wesselius and Central Statistics Bureau (CBS) introduce new MIT-index for Dutch high-tech sector. (p2)
- Dutch airfreighters' association NVVL expects airfreight will continue to grow in 1997. (p2)
- Amsterdam will not be polished up for the Euro summit in June, says city's mayor Schelto Patijn. (p3)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Spain's airline Iberia is seeking to form an alliance with Royal Dutch Airlines/KLM amongst others. (p1)
- The traditional 200 kms ice-skating marathon on the lakes between 11 towns is definitely going to take place. (p1)
- Korean ministry of trade announces there will no takeover of bankrupt aircraft maker Fokker by Samsung. (p3)
TROUW
- Car-drivers, smokers and house-owners will feel new taxation changes the most
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Local rates will go down for first time in years, but some owners may still pay more because of revaluation of their property. (p1)
- Green electricity's popularity is growing. (p11)
